notes: The plainest possible statement: an unformatted amount against one field.
turn: My salary this year is 1200000.

notes: Indian digit grouping plus a currency word. Step 7.1 measured that the model's own formatting is unstable, so normalisation is code.
turn: I earned Rs. 14,00,000 as salary.

notes: Rupee sign attached to the digits.
turn: My salary is ₹9,50,000.

notes: A multiplier word rather than digits.
turn: I make about 14 lakh a year from my job.

notes: Crore multiplier on the business head.
turn: My consultancy made a profit of 2 crore last year.

notes: The k multiplier, which people type far more often than they write lakh.
turn: I paid 45k as health insurance premium.

notes: A count, not an amount.
turn: I am 63 years old.

notes: Age follows from the turn by arithmetic but is not written in it.
turn: I retired at 58 and that was two years ago.

notes: A choice field stated in the enum's own word.
turn: I want to be taxed under the old regime.

notes: The other choice.
turn: I opted for the new tax regime this year.

notes: Residential status follows from the facts of presence; the term itself is never used.
turn: I have been living in Dubai for the last four years and only visit India for a week each year.

notes: The same field stated outright.
turn: I am a resident individual.

notes: A head of income that may be negative. A sign dropped here is a wrong tax.
turn: I have a loss of 250000 from my rented house after the interest deduction.

notes: The same head, positive, using the Act's own phrase.
turn: My income from house property is 3,00,000.

notes: Short-term gains, named explicitly.
turn: I made 80000 in short-term capital gains on shares.

notes: Long-term gains, named explicitly. The two heads are taxed differently, so confusing them is a correctness failure.
turn: Long-term capital gains of 2,50,000 from selling equity.

notes: A loss stated as a loss rather than as a negative number.
turn: I booked a short-term capital loss of 40,000.

notes: Interest is the commonest other-sources item.
turn: Bank interest of 32,000 this year.

notes: The section 123 deduction, named by its instruments rather than by any section number.
turn: I put 1,50,000 into PPF and LIC premiums.

notes: The section 126 deduction.
turn: Health insurance premium paid 25,000 for my family.

notes: Tax already paid, which is a credit and never a negative.
turn: TDS of 1,10,000 was already deducted from my salary.

notes: The other prepaid-tax field.
turn: I have paid 60,000 as advance tax so far.

notes: An assessment year: tax year = assessment year minus one (ADR-100).
turn: This is for assessment year 2026-27.

notes: The abbreviated assessment year, shifted back one (ADR-100), plus a second field in the same sentence.
turn: For A.Y. 2025-26 my salary was 8,00,000.

notes: Four fields in one line, each needing its own span.
turn: I am 35, resident, salary 18,00,000, and I paid 1,50,000 into ELSS.

notes: A terse telegraphic turn of the kind a returning user actually types, including a loss stated as a loss.
turn: Salary 22,00,000, house property loss 2,00,000, LTCG 1,20,000, TDS 3,50,000, new regime.

notes: Pension belongs to the salary head, which is a vocabulary mapping rather than a copy.
turn: I am 67, my pension is 6,00,000, I earn 1,80,000 interest, and I paid 50,000 for health insurance.

notes: Both regimes are named and neither is claimed. Extracting one here is a fabricated fact.
turn: What is the difference between the old and the new regime?

notes: A lawful-planning question rule 03 requires the system to answer, carrying no facts at all.
turn: Can I pay rent to my mother?

notes: A statutory question, not a personal statement.
turn: How is capital gains tax calculated on property?

notes: GST is outside the Act and outside the 15 fields. Forcing it into deduction_other would put a wrong number in the calculator.
turn: I also pay 35,000 a year in GST on my consultancy billings.

notes: Agricultural income is its own treatment and is not one of the heads modelled here.
turn: I received 5,00,000 as agricultural income from my farm.

notes: The model sees the masked turn, so any span crossing the PAN can only quote the mask.
turn: My PAN is ABCDE1234F and my salary is 11,00,000.

notes: Two fields either side of a masked token.
turn: My PAN is ABCDE1234F, I am 41 and my salary is 11,00,000.

notes: Paise. A float intermediate would lose them, which is why the value is a Decimal.
turn: I paid 2,50,000.50 in advance tax.

notes: The catch-all field, which exists so an unnamed deduction is not silently dropped.
turn: Other deductions of 75,000 that I claim.

notes: Which capital-gains head applies follows from the holding period; long-term is never stated.
turn: I sold a flat I had owned for eight years and made 12,00,000.

notes: The mirror of the non-resident case.
turn: I have been in India for the whole of the last ten years.

notes: A fractional multiplier beside an ordinary grouped amount.
turn: Salary 9.5 lakh, TDS 45,000.

notes: A turn with no content at all. The node must still return a well-formed object.
turn: Thanks, that helps.

notes: The business head as a loss.
turn: My business made a loss of 3,00,000 last year.

notes: An age stated outright beside a conclusion drawn from it; the conclusion is not a field.
turn: I turned 61 in April, so I am a senior citizen.
